capabilities: Open a codeblock's content in a configured external editor
Detect the codeblock language and create temporary files with matching extensions
Sync changes from the external editor back into the note
Configure the terminal and editor command via a JSON array
extras: Installation is manual (release files into .obsidian/plugins) or via cloning and building the repository; the manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The README mentions the plugin was implemented with the help of Claude Code.
motivation: The author wanted the autocompletion, auto-indent and LSP capabilities of Neovim when writing multi-line code snippets in notes.
problem: Editing multi-line code inside Obsidian lacks autocompletion, auto-indent and LSP features available in dedicated editors.

requires.name: an external editor (e.g. Neovim, VS Code) and optionally a terminal emulator

summary: Codeblock editor bridge that opens a codeblock's content in an external editor such as Neovim or VS Code and syncs edits back into the note.
